notes.title: Developers diaries #25
notes.content:
[h1]Diaries in video[/h1] [previewyoutube=rPM0KQjOKls;full][/previewyoutube] [h1]Diaries in text[/h1]Hi to everyone! Here are the developers of City Car Driving 2 speaking. 

We have taken into account the criticism that watching videos without sound is boring and makes little sense.  

And in log # 25, we are sharing the progress in the mechanics of cargo transportation and construction. Now we are approaching the key object in the game: this is a sawmill where resources are stored. 

In this building and other similar objects in the game world, we will be able to take various supplies, their list has not been approved, but all resources will be logical, only what passenger cars can transport. 

It is very important to note that the UI is now in working order: this is debugging information for us, the developers. This will definitely not happen in the game, it is important to show the mechanics here. 
Each resource has its own weight; they are gradually loaded into the vehicle and automatically stored in boxes. All this changes the physics of the car while driving: the car’s handling will obviously become more difficult, and it will grow noticeably heavier.

After reloading the resources, you can select any building on the map that requires construction. 
As an example, we chose a paint workshop building, you may notice “objects flying in the air”: this happened after we changed the coordinates of the entire map to adjust the traffic. 
In the workshop building, we do the same as in the sawmill – independently reload the supplies, and then we press the “construct” button. 

After this, through a standard loading screen with tips and history of the city, we finish the construction of the object. The key detail of this mechanic is that in the game world, there will be objects that only change their model, but there will also be buildings that are fully functional. For example, as you might guess, in this object, we will be able to paint our vehicles. 

This is a rather short diary, and this is still not the promised “DevMP4” section. Instead of the usual log in text, we are experimenting with the format of presenting the information about the progress of the development. Have your say, we equally accept wishes for success, criticism, and negative feedback. 

Thank you for your interest in the project and feedback. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e1587d01f1caf24e0bcc3396dce0d9b36a70038a.png[/img] Developer logs are published every two weeks, don’t miss them.

notes.content:
You will find only an extensive list of questions and answers. For your convenience, the questions are classified into categories. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/509dd38053625766ab552f711ba1879749a89103.gif[/img]
[h1]Important and Frequently Asked Q&A[/h1]
[list][*][b]Will we ever see multiplayer?[/b][*]
[i]We are aware that many of you want to see multiplayer, but at the moment unfortunately we don’t have the resources to fully implement it alongside with keeping up interest and performance for each player. We are still holding our position: we don’t rule out adding multiplayer mode in the future, but we can’t speak of exact dates yet.[/i]
[*][b]Are game pad, steering wheel, and other controllers supported? [/b]
[*] [i]Yes, they are. The game is mainly geared towards steering wheels, but the keyboard and mouse are still the most popular PC input devices, we can’t leave these out. [*][i]No support is expected for early access. Unfortunately, we don’t have the resources to implement full support, so we can’t make any promises.[/i]

[*] [i]Same deal as with TrackIR, though, chances of VR support are higher since we have already developed a VR mode in the original CCD. [/i]

Apart from the discord server, we will be improving our social media presence and be more open to the public. This has been taking a long time, since we are putting all our efforts into development, and interactions with the community other than our Developers’ Diaries and on-and-off exchanges in the comments are quite time-consuming[/i]
[*][b]Apart from exercises, will CCD 2.0 keep focus on abidance by Traffic Rules? [/b]

We would love to develop a prominent large-scale car simulator to take its market position, however, that would require much more financing than we have currently. This is why we are aiming for early access. Another reason is that we expect to receive your feedback and plan the upcoming release together.[/i]

notes.title: Developers diaries #22
notes.content:
After the New Year, our schedule got disrupted, and we began to publish the logs in the middle of our work on the game. So we had to write the logs before we finished what we were talking about. Therefore, this log comes out, breaking the usual pace. We don’t want to leave you without logs, but, as they say, we need to “optimize our processes” :)

After this log, we will return to our usual schedule – a log once every two weeks. 

Today, we’ll talk about how the development of very important aspects of the game is going: the first iterations of traffic behavior and tuning the car’s suspension.
[previewyoutube=6mKKc4F-ZRk;full][/previewyoutube] The video shows the first iterations of traffic. The first task facing our team in this direction was to merge our traffic system with UE. For this purpose, we created the simplest test model of a car – a “box,” reminiscent of a car in its shape

We faced many challenges: from differences in units of measurement and coordinate system to limitations in the simulation of solid state physics. Therefore, the first “cars” performed various stunts, at times driving with their wheels upside down and accelerating to incredible speeds.
[previewyoutube=i4P8uzL0V9Y;full][/previewyoutube] Now a pressing problem for us is the friction of car tires with the surface. UE’s physics engine, called “Chaos,” lacks flexibility and developer friendliness

In Log #21, you may have noticed that friction problems still persist. In the game, this is reflected in the periodic “slipping” of cars on any surface in the game. Also, in the video above, in addition to a vivid demonstration of problems with friction, we check “ragdoll” – physics (this will not happen in the game, these videos are old recordings).
[previewyoutube=DBfA6vp92nk;full][/previewyoutube]Here we look at the performance of the suspension: whether it is similar to the reference one or not, the key determination is the suspension travel. Then, the suspension is adjusted according to the data from the reference. Let’s take a closer look at how this happens.
[olist]
[*] We take a car in reality and create a similar car in the game without violating licensing rights. After that, we find information about the travel distance of the front and rear shock absorbers of the car. This will be the length of the shock absorber strut suspension.
[*] We set the coordinates for mounting the shock absorber strut based on the model. From the point of view of our physics, the mount is the point at which the center of the wheel will be when the suspension is fully compressed. If the lengths of the front and rear suspensions differ (as a rule, this is the case), then the mounting height of the longer suspension should be higher than that of the shorter one by the amount of the difference.
[*]We are looking for information about the stiffness of the front and rear springs (leaf springs) of the car. We set this stiffness in the car configuration file. If there is no data available, we calculate it: given the spring stiffness, we calculate its load. Stiffness in kg is multiplied by the acceleration of gravity and we get the value in Newtons. With this force, the car presses on the spring with its weight. For example, 337 kg (the stiffness of the front spring of the given car) * 9.8 = 3302 N. With this force, the car will press on the spring. Given the load, we calculate the stiffness coefficient.
[*]The stiffness coefficient is calculated using the formula: the spring load is divided by the suspension travel multiplied by 33 % of its compression. For example, 3302 / (0.155 * 0.33) = 64,555.
[*] Next, we set the damping coefficient as the stiffness coefficient divided by 10.
[*] We add a progression curve.
[*] We adjust the preload so that the compression of all suspensions at rest on a flat surface is 33 % +/- 5 %, since in reality manufacturers adjust the suspension 2/3 for compression and 1/3 for rebound. Increasing pretension reduces compression, decreasing it does the opposite.
[*] At the end, we check the height and evenness of the car, focusing on how the car behaves in reality (mainly from photographs and videos). An approximate correct result is when the bottom is parallel to the ground, and the ground clearance corresponds to the image of the car. As a rule, with the correct data and actions from the previous paragraphs, the car’s suspension is configured by this point. If it still doesn’t match a little, we adjust the damping and the mounting point of the strut “by eye.”
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e2e55676e9160fbc224806ff854de92987ebad7a.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]When is the full gameplay video coming?[/b]
[*] Work is still underway, and we cannot say exact dates. First of all, we must create the game. We try to share the development progress with you in as much detail as possible. Marketing the game is not an issue for us, so before we start actively advertising and showing the game, we want to make sure that we have made a great car simulator. 
[*] [b]Will trucks and buses be playable? [/b]
[*] No, they won’t be in Early Access for sure. Perhaps in the future, we will expand our fleet. 
[*][b] Will there be a career as a taxi driver? Passenger carrier? [/b]
[*] Not in the first Early Access version. As we noted in the New Year’s Roadmap, we put this issue aside to deepen other mechanics of the game. We plan to add a taxi driver career approximately in the second major patch for the game in Early Access. 
[*] [b]Will there be cockpit support like for sim racing? [/b]
[*] No, we are not a sim racing company and for us adding such support is an unjustified expense. 
[*] [b]Will there be an initial test to obtain a driver’s license? [/b]
[*] Yes, sure. As we mentioned in previous logs, without obtaining a work license, you will not be able to engage in some of the gaming activities. 
[*] [b]What about a full range of fines?[/b]
[*] Of course, there will be fines that you will need to pay because there will be an economy in the game. We couldn’t leave CCD 2.0 without fines: this is a key feature of the game. 
[*] [b]Thanks to changes in physics, will drifting be possible in the game? [/b]
[*] We do not encourage unsafe driving in any way, and we do not advise you to do so. (Yes, it will be possible, but how could it be otherwise, in a game about cars? :) There are no plans for rear-wheel drive player cars in the first version of Early Access, but we will add them in our first major patch. 
[*] [b]Will there be police implementation? [/b]
[*] Maybe. We didn’t look that far. If we decide to do this, it will definitely be before the game’s full release, but not in the first major patches.
[*] [b]What input device is the game being developed for first? In the previous videos, it appears that the recording is being done from the keyboard.[/b]
[*] First of all, we focus on steering wheels. We actually recorded most of the videos in the logs from the keyboard because it’s just more convenient for us, and we don’t position the logs as marketing materials.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e1587d01f1caf24e0bcc3396dce0d9b36a70038a.png[/img]
This log is a bit mixed in the topics, but today, we decided to simply share the features in the development of CCD 2.0. So at the end of the log, we attach a video of one of the first traffic launches.

notes.title: The release of the City Car Driving 2.0 has been moved to September 2024
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/50bc180f6df7d9578a2da19e4e413ea412de9814.png[/img]

It is already obvious to us that we have developed the basic gaming environment, but did not have time to fill it with content. At the moment, we are adding various missions and challenges so that, even in early access, the game differs from the first CCD. And so that, due to changes in the game formula, it does not feel like a “step back.” Also, mechanics related to the transport ecosystem require polishing. They are all connected with the economy, and we want to make them simple but good. They are fully functional, however, the economic factor in the game requires tying everything into a single fabric.

Based on the testing results, it turned out that the game optimization leaves much to be desired, and this does not meet our City Car Driving development standards. In addition, the game has bugs that should not be allowed in the game, even in the first early access version.

Additionally, there is a separate issue of setting up the compatibility of steering wheels, gamepads, keyboards and the mouse as the main input devices. Not only from the point of view that “they work” but also the ease of device use when playing.

Here is the main news:
[list][*] We will continue to publish developer logs in text format, but will soon add video format. In our first video, we want to show part of the prepared gameplay. The video version will be called «DevMP4», and will also be issued regularly – once every two weeks, from the day the first video is released. Fundamentally, the video version is not an advertisement. We want to show full gameplay so that a few months before the release of the game there is an understanding of what we created.[/list][list][*]Game price and system requirements will be announced with the first game trailer. We will announce the trailer date in advance.
[/list]We note in advance in order to prevent speculation: we have no crunches (overtime work), problems with the lack of resources or qualified specialists in the team, and anything else that can be described as “production hell.” We are well aware of our strengths and capabilities and are still focused on creating the best car simulator in existence.

Thus, the main reason for the postponement is to polish the game before its early access release so that you can fully enjoy our vision of the game.

Also, if you have ideas about what missions there might be in CCD 2.0, tell us. The best ones will be implemented in subsequent early access updates. Let’s build the game together.

Thank you for your understanding and support, good luck to everyone on real and virtual roads!

City Car Driving 2.0 development team

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/ac7de9035d4d617865f426c2841d67ebfdbc0dfc.png[/img]

notes.title: Developers diaries #12+1
notes.content:
We have never described the development sequence in the format of logs: what we did, how our work is progressing, and what will happen next. Only one of the logs was dedicated to how we started developing City Car Driving.

As was noted in the tenth log, we came to creating the game gradually: we collected various build options, tested engines.

In this log, we will talk about how we are working on CCD 2.0 after we have completed work with the prototype: how many people are in the team, what we have fully implemented, and what we is still in the making. 

After we got the prototype and confirmation for us that CCD 2.0 could be created, the very first thing we decided to create from scratch was the setting. We realized that many players expected an update to the first part, but we wanted to provide something new.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/4fa3ab765c1120603bf5806d76a962f6a95a5dd6.png[/img]
[h2]Setting | Location[/h2]
The very first thing our small team started to do was to conceptualize the main location that will open CCD 2.0. 

Of the many options, we chose the average option in the south of the Mediterranean with European traffic rules.

We made that decision because we wanted to reinvent the core CCD gaming formula.
The setting of the original CCD is Russia. Regardless of the change in the traffic rule base in the settings, the location did not change.

We didn’t really like this – it contradicted the first principle developed for us: everything should be authentic and not take away from the gameplay.

It is precisely because of the combination of our approach and the desire to try something new that CCD 2.0 opens in a Mediterranean location where it is eternal summer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/743dcd6699aded6a34a86a6fad3624c7d14e7fd5.png[/img]
At the same time, we realize that you are not likely to want to study the traffic rules of a specific country in which most players do not live. European road safety rules are very universal: they are similar to many rules in countries around the world (except for unique ones, such as Great Britain, for example), and in our idea, they should suit most players.

In the future, we plan to expand and add game locations: move from the abstract “European Mediterranean countries” to specific ones.

During development, we saw all your feedback, so the first thing we want to add is Russia. Only after the European and Russian regions are fully implemented, will we think about expanding the in-game geography.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Before we began to talk in detail in our Logs about what we were developing, it seemed that we were literally taking the original CCD, transferring it to a modern engine, remaking favorite locations and that’s it. In fact, along with developing the location, we designed the gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/694d9e029f93108362ccf38ec54f0e3dc7a64188.png[/img]
Combining two game modes into one turned the entire gameplay into one campaign. That entailed abandoning the capability for the player to customize the amount and density of traffic. Abandoning the free choice of weather conditions and time.

Instead, we are developing an environment that simulates a complete game world with its own rules and dynamic changes in weather and traffic. 

In addition to global changes in the weather, we reduced the scope of the driving school. CCD 2.0 retains the core exercises and exam. However, during development we removed many exercises. That needed to be compensated for with something: that’s how the “Quest Exercises” appeared. Cargo transportation is a logical continuation of what was in the original CCD. 

Also, all the infrastructure relevant to driving has been added.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/4dade8553fbb94f0a68acc95d1cd6a42790e9c6d.png[/img]
[h2]Team | How things are now[/h2]
Of course, in words, in the form of a small story, it looks like an excellent car simulator. Let’s go through the key points of the project in reality.

The concept of the gameplay, location, and basic mechanics was completed in mid-2022. After that, we started development.

By the start of 2023, we had the location and several basic mechanics roughly ready. We expected that we would be able to quickly talk about the development of the project, but our silence lasted for long six months: this is due to the fact that we put some of the mechanics on the back burner (we haven’t talked about them yet, everything mentioned in the logs will be available in the game). Part of the location also had to be removed.

Realizing that we had kept silent for too long, we filmed driving a car on the most finished street in the game: this became the first teaser for the game.

Then and now we did not start an advertising campaign. We share the development with the audience that we gathered over the years of the life of the original CCD and carefully select all the feedback; at this pace, we can create what we planned, manage to make changes to the project, and lay down opportunities for the future. 

After a long time of development, we decided to share a little information about ourselves, and at what stage our development is.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/4f5edf731c37fa56498da1543c46ab3dff45e879.png[/img]
[b]How many people are there on the team?[/b]
[i]Currently fifteen. Initially, CCD 2.0 was developed by no more than three.[/i] 

[b]How long has CCD 2.0 been in development?[/b]
[i]One and half year; before this, research was carried out, various prototypes were created.[/i]

[b]Is this a simulator or a game?[/b]
[i]Despite the fact that we are Forward and are developing City Car Driving 2.0, we are a separate division from the simulators and are creating specifically a game.[/i]

[b]Why will the game be released in early access?[/b] 
[i]We don’t have the budget to create a large-scale car simulator. As everyone knows, car simulators are not very popular in the gaming industry. The second reason is that we want to see your feedback and plan a future game together.[/i]

[b]Why the answer to many requests is “no, we won’t have it”?[/b]
[i]The type of the game has already been planned, so at the moment, we are creating the foundation for the future. We collect all reviews: about the drunk driver mode, and about Russia, and about traffic rules in the UK.[/i]

[b]What about the graphics?[/b]
[i]We have optimized the game for different devices. For example, the teaser was shot on “default” settings, not even on medium graphics settings. Since then, it has changed for the better. We constantly share the look of the game “at the moment,” so before the game is released in early access, we will definitely preview the final look of the graphics.[/i]

[b]Why are logs published only once every two weeks, and video formats, even short ones, have appeared not long ago?[/b] 
[i]We do not have a development or marketing team. All videos and screenshots are taken during the work of level designers. Most of the logs, which do not touch on a serious technical component, are written by our game designer. The tester carefully reads all the errors, and the project manager tries not to lose the semantic component by reading the log again before publication. We do all the logs in between our main work sessions.[/i]

[h2]What’s next?[/h2] 
We are finishing up the location, straightening up the gameplay, testing traffic, and finalizing the weather.

After that, we carefully polish the game for the remaining time and release it in early access. Part of the team, when they complete work on early access, will move on to creating the second half of the city, creating new game modes and tasks.

What we tell in the logs before the game release in early access is certainly not everything we planned. 
At the end of the log, we would like to specifically note that we see and collect all feedback and try to personally answer every question and comment. And you can also influence the game and its final appearance after early access.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e1587d01f1caf24e0bcc3396dce0d9b36a70038a.png[/img]
You can always find out more about the upcoming game before its release in the Developers Logs, regularly published every two weeks.

notes.title: Developers diaries #9
notes.content:
In the original City Car Driving, passenger transportation is the second important game activity. Just like cargo transportation, taxi driving has been significantly changed.

Passenger transportation is available at any time in the game, but thanks to many new features, taxi driving has a slightly different pace of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/1e6b64897f5cc91367b6559d3d59cdee43d13a80.png[/img]
To start taxi driving, you, as in the case of cargo transportation, just need to use the in-game phone. Differences in the game modes are already noticeable at this stage.

You have an application on your phone that is almost identical to real taxi booking and taxi driver applications. When you select this application, an interactive map of the city will appear on your phone, showing points with passengers.

For each passenger, the points to pick them up and to deliver are shown. In addition to these points, passenger rating will be shown. The rating is an indicator for you: which passengers are good and which are not; which will be easier or harder to deal with.

Each time you enter the taxi application, or complete an order, the location of customers will change. Unlike in the case of cargo transportation, you will not have the opportunity to choose your favorite route. For each new passenger transportation, it will be necessary to optimize and recreate the route.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/fcfb460d79aa87417677b5a3da54f961121ccfcf.png[/img]
In the first part of City Car Driving, passenger transportation was a full-fledged game mode, including due to such a parameter as “passenger mood”.

Thanks to your feedback and a lot of “how it works” guides from the community, we were able to take into account the errors in the implementation of the “passenger mood” mechanics in CCD2.

Now the system is implemented in the following way: each passenger has their own list of wishes and requirements. There are customers who are the least picky about your car. They practically do not react if you arrive in a damaged or dirty car, they do not care how long the trip lasted, and how many times you stopped at gas stations.

The mood counter is not as sensitive and does not cause you, for example, to lose all your trip progress if you do not turn on the turn signal when changing lanes.

Depending on the condition of your car, the style of the trip, as well as the passenger themselves, this parameter becomes more predictable at the beginning of the trip and clearly signals the actions that can and cannot be allowed in taxi driving.

If one may say so, now the parameter of mood has turned into a “difficulty curve” that is predictable and, most importantly, maintains interest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/9b32130dc56d7ff86b03af6057e0b8ea5620d9cc.png[/img]
[i]Taking this opportunity, in the topic about taxi driving, we will show the answer to one of the many comments: “The roads in the city are not uniform and include not only narrow streets.”[/i]

As with cargo transportation, there are various taxi modifiers that influence driving. And it’s not just the mood and requirements. Here are some examples:
[list]
[*] The passenger asks to stick to the average speed X and drive at it until the end of the trip 
[*] The passenger asks to reduce the speed to X and drive at it until the end of the trip 
[*] The passenger asks to pass through certain sections of locations
[*] The passenger asks to stop at a certain place before reaching the final destination
[*] The passenger can ask to pick up other passengers
[/list]While it is clear how all the modifiers influence the game, the last one listed should be reviewed in more detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/244578ee4a63117cf1399ee7b87478e9366a4bc4.png[/img]
In CCD 2.0, taxi driving is no longer limited to one passenger. Now you can choose a car for several passengers and pre-select orders with more than one customer. In this option, the mood counter is kept as one, but takes into account the desires of each passenger. Often, if you take an order for several people, several points appear at once where each person should be delivered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/bbb323201692207411b18548b5432d3ecef7fe58.png[/img]
[i]Work on the location is not yet fully completed. For example, our embankment is not ready. The entire street is at the concept stage.[/i]

All mechanics in total provide a different experience than working as a courier to transport goods. In the taxi driver mode, your pace of the game increases, and the difficulty of completing the task grows. All this happens gradually, depending on your skills. This system provides a comfortable pace of the game for novice drivers, and a worthy challenge for experienced motorists.

Each of the game modes described above is designed to give you a different driving experience.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e1587d01f1caf24e0bcc3396dce0d9b36a70038a.png[/img]
Developers Logs are published every two weeks. Don’t miss them!

notes.title: Developers diaries #3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c190664630e1cce9eb8c943ed60250b566ba30e0.png[/img]

As in the original City Car Driving, you will find a number of useful exercises that will help you master driving at a good level.

In CCD 2.0, the test circuit is designed from the point of view of the sequential passage of all exercises. At the same time, you will be able to independently choose the element that you want to study. 
The test circuit is an important part in the gameplay with somewhat expanded functionality, compared to the original CCD. The following options will be available on the test circuit:
[list]
[*] The ability to perform exercises to hone driving skills with subsequent scoring
[*] Practicing only those exercises in which you are interested, without a scoring system
[*] Going through the entire set of exercises with subsequent scoring
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/6ebb95980683a823fd02692de84dd89be8ab91b2.gif[/img]
[i]There are a lot of interactive objects on the test circuit, thanks to them, you will understand when you make a mistake.[/i]

Completing the assigned tasks leads to an exam in the city. For novice drivers, this system will help prepare themselves for full participation in the road traffic.

[b]#1 Hill entrance[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/da1de90cda671c1087317b5da44820360a0c16a6.gif[/img]
[i]At the test circuit, the hill is a high ground with a slope of 12°. According to all the requirements, we have to drive to the highest point, stop, and then carefully move out.[/i]

[b]#2 Cone slalom[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/744f1532cc7eae1666e34218097dc3d976bec4d8.gif[/img]
[i]An exercise in which you need to maneuver along an extremely smooth trajectory without touching the cones. Cone slalom is one of the most interesting classical exercises in preparation for driving in the city.[/i]

[b]#3 U-turn in a restricted space[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/0820629ed87173e85cd45390e32b42bf9f2b7fca.gif[/img]
[i]We are approaching difficult exercises, at this point, you will need to really feel your vehicle.[/i]

[b]#4 Rear entrance to the box[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e024437b3520fbaa0a4b914a941ce16583a0de65.gif[/img]
[i]An exercise fixing maneuvering skills that helps to finally get used to the dimensions of the vehicle.[/i]

[b]#5 Parallel parking[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/7dcdf77df494db71083187a316fe5aab8afb3578.gif[/img]
[i]This exercise is a little test of all your driving skills. For more immersion in the process, there are car mock-ups simulating real road users on the test circuit.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c281d65958c243f8151f28da528a3df99209c552.png[/img]

[b]In addition to exercises, will the emphasis on compliance with traffic rules be maintained in CCD 2.0?[/b] 
[i]Yes, we consider traffic rules to be one of the important components of the gameplay, and we try to deepen the interaction of the player and traffic rules.[/i]

[b]Will the sounds be like in the original CCD or modified?[/b]
[i]With the transition to UE, the sounds in the game will be changed.[/i]

[b]What will happen to the original CCD?[/b]
[i]It will remain with the players, in the form they are used to, we do not replace, and even more so we do not take the game away from people. We do not exclude the possibility of the release of small updates for the original City Car Driving, but now all forces are concentrated on the development of City Car Driving 2.0.[/i]

[b]Is Steam Workshop support planned?[/b]
[i]Yes, it is. We want to give people the opportunity to share their own modifications with maximum convenience.[/i]

[b]Will it be possible to flexibly adjust the traffic density, the number of pedestrians, weather conditions as in the original CCD?[/b]
[i]No, we are trying to give a new experience to all users, so we are trying a different approach.[/i]

[b]Is it planned to introduce motorcycles in CCD 2.0?[/b]
[i]In early access – definitely not.[/i]

[b]Is the system of fatigue, hunger, and so on planned?[/b]
[i]No, we consider this an extra complication for a real and living person who needs to rest and eat themselves, especially when playing a car simulator, where you need to concentrate your attention.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/56ca34bd6f3e28da6287d69f380147de5e830e83.png[/img]
In the next issue, we will talk a little about the game world, show some screenshots of locations, and talk about the approach to level design.

Dev diaries are released every two weeks, where we are talking in detail about the development of the game. Don’t miss them!

notes.title: Developers diaries #2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e3a1aa7336a4b271b30e227f3cd89e98c6cf4c47.png[/img]

When it became clear to us that the original City Car Driving engine was very outdated, we began to look for a new solution that would be:
[list]
[*] Actually developing and interesting for specialists.
[*] Scalable, which would be suitable not only for a new game, but also could be used in the future for our simulators.
[*] Optimized for modern computers.
[/list]
Our search stopped at the Unreal Engine, first of all because of its flexibility in operation and the variability of tools that allow artists and designers to perform many tasks independently. In addition to these reasons, the undoubted advantage of UE is its compatibility with our internal editors: landscape, traffic, and so on.

About a year ago, we created a pilot project on UE4, used internally, after which we transferred all our developments to UE5 in CCD 2.0



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f61727afc3b927fa5754fc0a5804e19b3e0f334d.png[/img]

Let’s start by creating a landscape. The main part of the landscape and roads are created by a generator specially developed by us, which is not part of the UE. Using the same generator, the main AI of urban traffic is created, as well as the logic of pedestrians. As a mandatory feature, traffic control is attached to this. A side part of the landscape is completed by artists as 3D models. With this approach, we can ensure for ourselves a high speed of creating locations with an extensive network of roads and a realistic landscape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/4b90c4043f359a232c2669198db687b35926b59c.png[/img]
[i]The screenshot shows how the location is filled: objects without textures and detailing are a blockout (a blank for an object). Level designers, when filling the location, work in parallel with viewing the physical properties of the location so that there are no holes or invisible walls. After filling the location, the objects are checked for a collision with the player’s car.[/i]

IWhen filling the location with objects, we use internal developments for automatic placement and generation. In the development process, designers and artists use industry-standard optimization methods:
[list]
[*] Levels of Detail (both manual and automatic).
[*] Geometry Instancing.
[*] Material Instancing.
[*] Combining textures into atlases (both manual combination and automatic when creating HLOD groups).
[/list]
PBR (Physically Based Rendering) materials are used on the objects with the possibility of their customization by level designers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/2764f9d553e7924a7a4e8761c4cba2ae848cabd0.png[/img]
[i]Reflections in the game work on the basis of PBR materials (Roughness-metalness). Thus, materials without roughness have a reflectivity. At the same time, the reflections themselves are generated using SSR (screenspace reflections) technology.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/96e6e2fd9626e2125356e69a6b6b1c123443dbe2.png[/img]
[i]To make the above reflections more realistic, we have added reflections based on HDR (High Dynamic Range) on the car. The reflection capture mode is displayed on the right side of the screenshot. The mode displays the calculation of reflections in real time, this is the main technology that draws reflections on textures.[/i]

At the very beginning of development and at every stage, from the first polygon to the last pixel, we were focused on maximizing the optimization of the game. At the same time, we try to achieve graphics quality that meets the industry standards, adjusted for the chosen style.

UE allowed us to choose one of two types of shading – Forward Rendering or Deferred Rendering. Forward is faster in some cases but makes it impossible to use many effects, reduces the overall performance and quality of dynamic lighting. Thus, in order to maintain the balance of the availability of modern graphic technologies, the speed of work and the capabilities for optimizing the final image, we settled on the Deferred Shading.

Having decided on the type of shading, we moved on to the basic lighting settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/cf3f7b81f9d44bda690f87293afb0f24cc6581c7.png[/img]
[i]It was decided to make the change of the time of day dynamic, so the intensity of the color of the sun and the filling light will be changing. Further, when determining the presence of dynamic light sources (lampposts, illuminated signs, interiors), performance measurement tests were carried out. The measurement results showed that it is necessary to combine different lighting methods – realtime (from light sources in the engine) and baked (glow within the texture).[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/2d2462e90e2c59f3405eb85ad7f381a3da2e66d7.png[/img]
[i]Shadows iare implemented using various UE lights functions and baked shadows at the model level. For example, “cascade shadows” work near the player. The shadow processing mode is shown on the right side of the screenshot. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/915d3e2b4b07702cb80eefcc27ca475820a4713a.png[/img]
[i]At a distance, cascading shadows disappear and DistanceField Shadows, much lighter for the performance, turn on.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c281d65958c243f8151f28da528a3df99209c552.png[/img]

[b]Will there be different regions, countries, etc. in CCD 2.0? [/b]
[i]In early access, we plan to release only one region: a southern city near the sea, in the future we plan to expand and add game locations.[/i]

[b]In CCD 2.0. will there be an imitation of damages to the car, after which it loses its functionality?  [/b]
[b]It will be, in future diaries we will definitely tell you how we want to implement this functionality. [/b]

[b]Will there be cars from the original CCD in 2.0?[/b] 
[i]No, we want to preserve the uniqueness of the products and will not mix vehicles. There will only be new cars in CCD 2.0.[/i]

[b]Will there be TrackIR support? [/b]
[i]At the moment, support is not being considered. [/i]

[b]Will there be VR support?[/b] 
[i]There will be no support in early access.[/i] 

[b]Will there be an expansion of social interaction with the audience? For example, a discord server, for the opportunity to discuss the game, or to communicate directly with the developers? [/b]
[i]Yes, it will. At the moment, we are preparing a discord server, and as soon as we are ready to launch it, we will immediately inform everyone.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/6bdba1cb8cb5c34a29d21fdee0c5cb1ac0999f88.png[/img]
